verdicts.strongest_argument: The document itself was picked up and written up by a retail-facing filing aggregator on the day it was filed: StockTitan's LSAK filing feed carries a 2026-09-01 headline, 'Lesaka (NASDAQ: LSAK) investor readies secondary share sale', naming IFC African, Latin American and Caribbean Fund, LP, the 857,362 shares and J.P. Morgan Securities as broker. That is not obscure — it is the same feed that covered the April 144 and the March/April/June ALAC Form 4s, so the IFC exit programme has been on the public tape continuously since at least 2026-03-04, including a 13D/A on 2026-06-17 itemising 671,112 shares sold on 22 dates. Two further points cut against the hunter's framing rather than the fact. First, 857,362 is exactly 1% of the 85,736,223 shares outstanding, i.e. the mechanical Rule 144 ceiling that essentially every affiliate files at — 'exactly the cap' is boilerplate, not a signal of urgency. Second, the baseline's own tape refutes the mechanism: the seller was, on the hunter's own reconstruction, absent from 2026-08-08 to 2026-09-01, and that is precisely the window in which the stock fell (run_up_20d = -5.38%) while the 5-day run-up with the seller allegedly back on the tape is +2.24%. If the presence of ALAC drove the price, the signs are backwards. Finally the direction is ambiguous even if the supply is real: after the March-August sales ALAC's residual is roughly a million shares, so a further 857k tranche largely retires a six-month overhang, which is as easily read bullish as bearish. And a Form 144 is a supply fact, not information about tonight's numbers.

prior_publication.what_it_says: StockTitan's LSAK filing feed headlines the Form 144: IFC African, Latin American and Caribbean Fund, LP filed to sell up to 857,362 common shares through J.P. Morgan Securities LLC.
The Form 144 itself, on public EDGAR, listing 857,362 shares and 35 prior sales between 2026-06-08 and 2026-08-07.
13D/A disclosing ALAC's 671,112 shares sold between 2026-03-18 and 2026-06-17 and the IFC group's remaining ~10.09% — the same continuous exit programme.
Prior LSAK Form 144 covered by the same aggregator, showing this filer's sales are routinely surfaced to retail within a day.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: run_up_20d_pct = -5.38% covers the window in which the seller was supposedly capped out and off the tape, while run_up_5d_pct = +2.24% covers the week the seller is said to have returned — the tape moves against the claimed mechanism. avg_volume_20d of 83,297 means the tranche is ~16% of daily volume if spread over the three-month 144 window, not 10x anything on any single day.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: Evidence that this tranche is being executed as a block or accelerated into the print rather than dribbled at the 1% pace, or a Form 4 showing outsized daily prints in the days immediately after 2026-09-02.

verdicts.strongest_argument: Both halves of the arithmetic are the company's own published numbers. The nine-month net loss attributable to Lesaka of $461 thousand, the R3,532,856 thousand goodwill balance and the equity figure are all in Exhibit 99.1 to the 2026-05-06 8-K, and management's FY26 positive-net-income promise is in the same release, on the 2026-05-07 call, and restated in at least four transcript outlets and in GlobeNewswire wire copy. The subtraction that turns those two published facts into 'Q4 must clear +$0.46m' is one line of arithmetic that any reader of the release can do, and management pre-announced its conclusion — they told the market the milestone would be achieved in Q4, which only makes sense if nine months were negative. The framing also overstates the fragility: Q3 itself delivered positive net income at the upper end of guidance with adjusted EBITDA +45% and adjusted EPS +247%, so a $0.46m Q4 swing is a low bar on run-rate, not a coin flip. What is genuinely undrawn is the goodwill leg — I could find no article, note or filing anywhere connecting the 30 June annual test on ~$207m of goodwill to the profitability promise, and the only prior impairment I can source is $7.0m in fiscal 2023 per the FY2024 10-K. That is a real, unpublished tail: a non-cash impairment is the one thing that could break the headline while leaving guidance-basis EBITDA intact. But it is also a generic risk-factor item disclosed in every 10-K, there is no observable trigger (the stock sits +23% off its 52-week low with EBITDA compounding), and if it lands most holders will read through a non-cash charge to the adjusted numbers the company guides on. Hence mid-range rather than low: published facts, trivial arithmetic, one unpublished but low-probability tail.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Company's own Q3 FY2026 release carrying the nine-month $461k net loss attributable to Lesaka, the R3,532,856k goodwill balance, and the guidance that FY2026 net income attributable to Lesaka will be positive.
Wire release: upper end of profitability guidance achieved, FY26 adjusted EPS raised to ZAR 5.50-6.00.
Transcript repeating that FY2026 will be the first profitable year on net income without exclusions since Lesaka's creation four years ago.
FY2024 10-K describing the annual goodwill impairment testing regime and the $7.0m of goodwill impaired in fiscal 2023.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: No dated move to attach: the facts entered the record on 2026-05-06/07, and the 2026-05-06 reaction was +1.43% and the 2026-05-18 headline-earnings correction +3.44% — the market read the Q3 package as mildly good, not as a fragile-profitability warning. No option chain exists to check whether downside is bid.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A source showing Lesaka's reporting-unit fair values ran close to carrying value at the last test, or an interim signal (Merchant division impairment indicators, a SENS trading statement) that a Q4 write-down is actually coming.

verdicts.strongest_argument: Every component of this claim is separately published, and three of the four are in wire or mainstream copy. The pre-commitment is a direct quote from the 2026-05-07 call — that at the September end-of-year presentation Lesaka would provide FY2027 guidance and a three-year medium-term outlook, 'inclusive of Bank Zero' given the expected completion — and it appears in the Investing.com transcript the hunter cites plus Motley Fool, Yahoo Finance, Insider Monkey and Globe and Mail write-ups of the same call. The non-completion is not obscure either: the 2026-06-11 long-stop extension from 2026-08-06 to 2027-01-31, with Prudential Authority approval outstanding, was filed as an 8-K and covered on 2026-06-17/18 by BusinessDay, TechCentral, ITWeb, MyBroadband, BusinessTech, The Citizen, Globe and Mail and StockTitan. The ~12% fully diluted issuance plus up to R91m cash has been in the deal's public description since the 2025-06-27 announcement, and 'Bank Zero turns profitable the year after completion' is management's own published framing. So the only thing the hunter adds is the join — that a guidance package promised 'inclusive of Bank Zero' now has to be delivered with the deal unclosed — and that join is available to any reader who saw both June headlines. It is also directionally two-sided: a first-ever three-year outlook is as plausibly a positive catalyst as a disappointment, and the fact that no completion 8-K exists is a negative-space observation the market already made when the long-stop moved. I searched the JSE/SENS route as well and found no August 2026 announcement; the most recent SENS item I can source is the 2026-05-18 headline-earnings correction, so nothing there is unpublished either.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Q3 call transcript: at the September end-of-year presentation Lesaka will give FY2027 guidance and a three-year medium-term outlook inclusive of Bank Zero.
Business Day reports the long-stop extension to 31 January 2027 with Prudential Authority consent still outstanding.
TechCentral on the same extension, agreed 11 June 2026, from 6 August 2026.
The 8-K itself, covered on the US filing feed: deal deadline pushed to January 31, 2027.
Company press release distributed to North American investors announcing the extension for approvals.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: The extension became public on 2026-06-17/18, well outside the 20-day run-up window, so nothing in run_up_5d (+2.24%) or run_up_20d (-5.38%) is attributable to it — it was absorbed nearly three months ago. No option chain, so no skew argument either way.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: Evidence that Prudential Authority approval has been granted or refused since June, or a source showing consensus still models FY27 with Bank Zero consolidated from Q1.

interactions: Findings #1 and #2 rest on the same disclosure package — the 2026-05-06/07 Q3 FY2026 release and call. #1 uses its statement of operations, #2 uses its call transcript, and both ultimately trade on the same 'FY26 is the first profitable year, and the next leg is Bank Zero' narrative management has repeated at every print since Q1 FY26. Counting them as two independent unpriced facts double-counts one publication event and one story. They also share a resolution date: the goodwill test (#1) and the Bank Zero-inclusive guidance (#2) are both settled by the same 30 June year-end close and the same document that lands tonight. Finding #0 is independent in its document (the Form 144), but its prior-sales table and the 2026-06-17 13D/A cited in support are the same selling programme reported twice, so its 'three tranches' should be read as one continuous six-month exit rather than three separate events. #0 is also internally two-sided against itself: the same filing that establishes the supply also implies ALAC's residual stake is close to exhausted after this tranche, which is the end of an overhang, not the start of one — the hunter takes only the bearish read.
concessions: The one thing I could not find published anywhere, in US wires, on EDGAR beyond the raw statements, or on the JSE/SENS stream, is any connection between the 30 June annual goodwill test on ~$207m of goodwill and the razor-thin FY26 profitability promise (part of #1). That link is genuinely undrawn; I discount it for low probability and non-cash character, not for publication.
